name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 204 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 44% fewer than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
status.nb: 204 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 44 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Hyderabad.

summary.en: Security forces are intensifying area domination exercises in Bandipora and Sopore along the Wullar axis while IGP Sujit Kumar warns that a single local terrorist remains active in Kashmir, sustaining the terror threat. In Manipur, hundreds rallied in Ukhrul demanding an end to ethnic violence and the SoO pact, Naga groups petitioned the prime minister for a political solution, and a Manipur PLA militant operating under a fake identity was arrested in Delhi. Maoist units in Chhattisgarh's Bijapur forest have hidden large caches, prompting forces to recover 711 grenade shells and a 5 kg pressure-cooker IED. The UCDP recorded 437 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Sikkerhetsstyrker intensiverer område-dominansøvelser i Bandipora og Sopore langs Wullar-aksen, mens IGP Sujit Kumar advarer om at en enkelt lokal terrorist fortsatt er aktiv i Kashmir og opprettholder terrortrusselen. I Manipur samlet hundrevis seg i Ukhrul og krevde en slutt på etnisk vold og SoO-avtalen, Naga-gruppene sendte en petisjon til statsministeren om en politisk løsning, og en Manipur-PLA-militant som opererte under en falsk identitet ble arrestert i Delhi. Maoist-enheter i Chhattisgarh-s skog i Bijapur har skjult store lager, noe som har fått styrkene til å gjenvinne 711 granatkapsler og en IED med 5 kg trykkoker. UCDP registrerte 437 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
